killReason: The need is real (DocuClipper from $29 a month, ProperSoft from $19.99 a month) but at least four free in-browser, no-upload converters already do exactly this job (Statement Extract free forever unlimited, Ledgerbridge, FileTailored, Somacon for IIF), and QuickBooks Online imports CSV natively. Our pitch of in-browser, nothing uploaded is already the free incumbents pitch, and organic search, our only allowed channel, is crowded with them. Same failure pattern as earlier ideas: free tools already do the job and there is no channel.

evidence.claim: DocuClipper sells CSV to QBO conversion from $29 a month for 60 pages.
ProperSoft sells its CSV2QBO converter with plans from $19.99 a month.
A QuickBooks community user asks for a CSV to QBO converter, saying the independent ones are not very good; a reply points to a $60 converter.
Ledgerbridge has a guide for users whose bank only offers CSV downloads and need a QuickBooks file, showing the problem is searched for.

nextAction: None. Killed at validating; no business case or spec needed.

evidenceAgainst.claim: Statement Extract offers a CSV to QBO converter it describes as free forever, unlimited transactions, running entirely in the browser.
Ledgerbridge offers a free in-browser CSV to QBO, QFX and OFX converter with no upload and per-bank pages, with only a one-time $29 Pro upgrade for unlimited rows.
FileTailored offers a CSV to QBO converter that it says runs locally in the browser with a free try button.
Somacon offers a free, unlimited in-browser CSV to IIF converter for QuickBooks Desktop.
QuickBooks Online itself accepts 3 or 4 column CSV bank uploads directly, so Online users need no QBO file.
Search results for free CSV to QBO converters already hold several free no-upload clones alongside paid vendors, so the only allowed channel, organic search, is crowded.
